newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-HAALAND SET TO LEAVE FOREST FOR ITALY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HAALAND SET TO LEAVE FOREST FOR ITALY.

text.p: Relegation-threatened English premier league club Nottingham Forest accepted on Wednesday that Alf-Inge Haaland will leave the City Ground at the end of the season.
Forest have offered the Norwegian international a lucrative new contract to extend his three-year stay with the club, but now seem certain to lose him to Italian side Napoli in the summer.
The 24-year-old midfielder becomes a free agent at the end of the season and has made contact with agents acting for the Italians, informing them he is keen to listen to what is on offer.

Forest general manager Dave Bassett has been told that Haaland will not be making a decision on his future until the summer, but his refusal to sign a new deal before Thursday's transfer deadline indicates he is ready to leave.
"There is nothing we can do because of the Bosman rule," said Bassett. "We've offered him a new contract and we want him to stay, but under freedom of contract he's holding all the aces."
Forest are in the relegation zone, third-from-bottom in the league, and have played more games than all their rivals.
